newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem makes Peronist whip new small business czar.
newsitem.headline: Menem makes Peronist whip new small business czar.

text.p: Argentina's Peronist President Carlos Menem said Thursday that his chief whip in the lower house of Congress, Jorge Matzkin, will head a new Department of Small and Medium-Sized Businesses.

"As soon as he is in Buenos Aires I will call him and offer him this job," said Menem. "We are permanently promoting small and medium-sized businesses and we want an organism that brings them all together."

The new department is the outcome of a debate between Economy Minister Roque Fernandez and Eduardo Duhalde, governor of Buenos Aires Province and the main contender to stand for president for the Peronists when Menem's term ends in 1999.

Duhalde had called for a "Production Ministry" to foment industrial activity and combat high unemployment. He also made digs at Fernandez's "orthodox" free-market policies which he said were out of date.
Fernandez shed his usual low profile last week to refute Duhalde's arguments and Menem, who is engaged in a subtle battle of wills with Duhalde, backed his economy minister.

"As long as I am president, we will not create a ministry of production. In a country which is growing at eight percent, exporting in an incredible fashion and importing capital goods in order to modernize its productive apparatus, I don't see the need for a production ministry," said Menem Thursday.
Matzkin's term as head of the Peronist majority in the Chamber of Deputies ends in October. The new department he will head will report directly to the presidency.
